decisions.reason: The dismantling joint is a core pipeline fitting that builds on existing welding and fabrication capabilities, and infrastructure demand is steady, so it likely meets aspirations and gives no cause for problemistic search.

The pipe support bracket fits the established infrastructure range at low incremental cost, though the earlier withdrawal of the similar bracket B suggests some risk that brackets fall short of aspirations.
The powder-coated waste bin is distant from the core and its results are uncertain, but it uses the existing coating equipment and slack from a growing industry lets the firm carry it for now.

The bin-with-ashtray line uses existing powder-coating and fabrication capacity and serves municipal customers the firm already reaches, so absent a clear shortfall the firm keeps it while it judges performance.

The outdoor ashtray line is the most distant diversification and the most likely to miss aspirations, but its low cost on shared coating equipment and the firm's slack argue for keeping it a while longer.
